title: POC weekly sync - model pinning & fallbacks
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results across candidate models, finalize model version pinning strategy, and confirm rollback/fallback policies. SE presented latency/cost tradeoffs and a proposed pin + fallback config. Customer asked for an A/B plan and request for formal benchmark spreadsheet and pricing. Agreed next steps: Redwood to run a runbook benchmark for the traffic profile, share security docs and updated pricing, and schedule canary rollout next week.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-01
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~43 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Natarajan (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (CTO - Catalyst Systems), Diego Ramos (ML Engineer), Sanjay Patel (Product)
---
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is our weekly POC sync. quick roll call?
[00:07] Maya Chen: Hi Jordan, hi Priya, Maya here.
[00:09] Diego Ramos: Diego, ML eng.
[00:11] Sanjay Patel: Sanjay, product.
[00:13] Priya Natarajan: Priya from Redwood SE, thanks team.
[00:16] Jordan Lee: Cool. Agenda today: review the benchmark runs we did, discuss model selection and pinning strategy, talk fallbacks and rollback, then agree next steps. Priya you wanna start with the numbers?
[00:28] Priya Natarajan: Yeah sure. so we ran the two configurations you asked: v1.2 quantized 8-bit and v1.3 float16, both on the same dedicated host profile. We used your sample set Diego sent (about 800 prompts), ran at 8 concurrent workers to approximate your burst.
[00:44] Priya Natarajan: Results summarized: v1.2-8bit p95 latency 185ms, avg token cost 0.0031 USD, v1.3-fp16 p95 140ms but cost ~0.0048 USD per token. Memory was fine on both with kv cache enabled, although we saw occasional higher GC spikes on v1.3 during long histories.
[01:05] Diego Ramos: quick question: when you say token cost, is that redwood per-token charge or infra cost estimate?
[01:10] Jordan Lee: That's the Redwood unit cost estimate including hosting. we break it down in the spreadsheet. we'll send full breakout.
[01:15] Sanjay Patel: The latency diff is noticeable. Our product needs median <120ms for snappy UX, but p95 can be higher for long contexts.
[01:24] Maya Chen: Yeah, we care about cost too since this pilot will scale to ~10M requests/mo if we go prod. so we need a compromise.
[01:33] Priya Natarajan: Right, so recommendation from SE: pin v1.2-8bit as primary for now to meet cost targets with a fallback to v1.3-fp16 when latency budgets allow or for high-quality responses for complex queries. Also propose an automatic fallback on model errors or elevated latency.
[01:48] Diego Ramos: How deterministic is behavior across these versions? We saw some prompt drift between v1.1 and v1.2 in earlier runs.
[01:56] Priya Natarajan: There can be differences — quantization changes can affect tokenization and subtle behavior. We recommend flagging a small eval set to detect regressions post-pin. Redwood has eval hooks so we can run continuous quality checks.
[02:11] Jordan Lee: Also about rollbacks — we suggest a canary rollout: 5% traffic on pinned v1.2 with fast rollback policy to previous stable. If we detect quality drop or increased hallucinations, auto-failover to the fallback model.
[02:25] Maya Chen: Auto-failover is good. How do we configure the thresholds?
[02:29] Priya Natarajan: We can set thresholds on latency p95, error rates, and eval score delta. Example: p95 > 250ms for 2 consecutive mins triggers fallback, or eval score drop more than 3% on the validation set triggers a rollback. We'll share suggested thresholds but you can customize.
[02:49] Diego Ramos: On the validation set, can we run the eval in shadow mode before switching? we want to see distribution differences.
[02:55] Priya Natarajan: Yes. Redwood supports shadow routing — run new model in parallel on same requests without impacting users, collect metrics, then decide. That's safe for canary.
[03:05] Sanjay Patel: On the security front, Maya asked about KMS and audit logs last week; any updates?
[03:11] Jordan Lee: Yep. We attached SOC2 snapshot in the playbook; we also support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated and we log request-level metadata for auditing. I'll share the short KMS integration note after the call.
[03:22] Maya Chen: Good. For data residency, we need EU-only processing for some clients; can Redwood pin region-specific hosts?
[03:29] Priya Natarajan: Yes, you can pin model instances to regions, and Dedicated hosts can be provisioned in target regions. We'll include region config options in the canary plan.
[03:38] Jordan Lee: Back to models — Diego, you mentioned prompt drift earlier. Do you have a small set of prompts we should use for regression tests?
[03:44] Diego Ramos: I can curate 200 prompts that reflect edge cases and long-context flows. will send by end of day tomorrow.
[03:50] Priya Natarajan: Great. We'll wire those into the eval. Also ran a quick test on fallback latency — switching to fallback model adds about 30-40ms overhead because of routing and cold-start if model isn't warmed. so recommend keeping a warm pool for the fallback.
[04:05] Sanjay Patel: What's the cost impact of warm pool?
[04:08] Priya Natarajan: It's about 10-15% of peak cost depending on the size of reserved capacity; we'll model it in the price sheet.
[04:15] Maya Chen: Pricing ask — can you show Dedicated commit vs hosted per token over 10M monthly requests?
[04:22] Jordan Lee: Yes, that's in the pricing draft. I'll update with the benchmark numbers and a Dedicated commit scenario.
[04:29] Diego Ramos: One more note: quantized models sometimes produce changed tokenization at boundary cases causing downstream parsing errors. We need to test structured output.
[04:38] Priya Natarajan: Good call. We'll include structured output tests as part of the eval harness.
[04:43] Jordan Lee: Anything on fallbacks beyond model-level? We have regional fallbacks and tiered capacity fallbacks too.
[04:49] Priya Natarajan: Right. We can have routing policy: primary model in US-east, fallback to smaller cheaper model in other region, or degrade to cached responses for known prompts to preserve UX. Caching prefix is useful for deterministic prompts.
[05:01] Sanjay Patel: How often would we need to refresh the prefix cache?
[05:04] Priya Natarajan: Depends on prompt churn, but we recommend TTL of 24-72 hours or manual invalidation on model updates.
[05:11] Maya Chen: Can we automate invalidation on pin changes?
[05:14] Priya Natarajan: Yes, Redwood exposes hooks to invalidate cache when you deploy a new pin.
[05:18] Jordan Lee: Ok, next let's talk timeline. We need final pin decision by next Wed to start canary the following week. Does that align?
[05:25] Maya Chen: We can do that if benchmarks and cost look good.
[05:28] Diego Ramos: I'll get the 200 edge prompts and concurrency profile by EOD tomorrow.
[05:31] Jordan Lee: Great. Priya, items for SE?
[05:34] Priya Natarajan: I'll run the 1k benchmark across v1.2-8bit, v1.3-fp16, and an alternative-lite model (smaller size) to show tradeoffs. I'll also prepare the canary/rollback playbook and share the spreadsheet. Expect results by Wed.
[05:49] Sanjay Patel: Can we also see an A/B plan? we'd like to evaluate quality difference on live traffic.
[05:53] Jordan Lee: Yes, we can do an A/B with 10/90 split for a week, capture business metrics and eval deltas. we'll include that in the plan.
[05:59] Maya Chen: On compliance, small ask — can you confirm what fields are logged? we need to ensure PII isn't stored in logs for some datasets.
[06:07] Priya Natarajan: We log metadata and anonymized request hash by default; for sensitive workloads we can disable request payload logging and set up audit-only trails with customer-controlled KMS. We'll include the config options in the KMS note.
[06:20] Jordan Lee: Ok wrapping up. Quick recap of next steps: Jordan to send pricing and security docs, Priya to run benchmarks and canary playbook, Diego to provide prompts and concurrency, Maya to confirm success criteria. We'll reconvene same time next week.
[06:33] Maya Chen: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[06:35] Diego Ramos: Thanks.
[06:36] Sanjay Patel: Thanks all.
[06:37] Jordan Lee: Thanks, bye.
